notes:
Two pieces from the v1.0.21 deferred list — the Discord bot's runtime listener and MT5 auto-detect.

### Discord bot now actually reads messages

v1.0.21 shipped the OAuth + 'Install TradingSupport Bot' flow. v1.0.22 wires up the runtime listener that reads messages in the channels you grant access to and forwards trading signals into TradeSpace. Bot token comes from the build-time-baked DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN; the listener auto-scopes to whichever Discord server you installed the bot in. Auto-restarts with exponential backoff (5s → 10s → … → 5min cap) on any gateway disconnect / network blip / token rotation.

If you already installed the bot on v1.0.21, it'll start listening as soon as you upgrade — no extra setup. If you haven't installed yet, head to the Bridge tab in the dashboard and click Install TradingSupport Bot.

### MT5 auto-detect on the Connect modal

Click the disconnected MT5 row in the Bridge tab — instead of asking you to type credentials, TradeSpace now scans your machine for MT5 installations and detects whether a terminal is currently running with an account logged in. Three states the modal renders:

1. Running terminal detected → big Connect this account button + DEMO or LIVE badge sourced from the live mt5.account_info() response. No password needed because TradeSpace attaches via mt5.initialize() with no args (AlreadyLoggedIn mode — the same path the engine already used).
2. MT5 installed but not running → list of detected installs (broker name + path) + 'open MT5 first, then Retry'.
3. Nothing on disk → install link to metatrader5.com + manual-form fallback under Config → MT5.

MT5 stores account credentials in encrypted blobs only the running terminal can decrypt — there's no plaintext file we could scrape for 'available logins' without reverse-engineering. The running-terminal probe + install enumeration is the honest auto-detect path.
